argument_summary: The strongest supportable position on the current admissible record is not that the merchant-dispute gap is immaterial or resolved, but that certification can be defended only as a narrow aggregate-readiness decision: aggregate launch readiness clears threshold by 2.3 points, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the public governance materials support deployment with documented limitations, evaluation results, and ongoing monitoring. That said, the same admissible record also shows the merchant dispute support segment misses target by 1.4 points, is named in two marketplace renewal commitments, and remains under open legal review for disclosure. The packet should therefore preserve the contrary record and avoid any claim of clean policy satisfaction.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the quarter-end rollout path. That cost does not change the policy standard, but it supports handling the issue through a bounded caveat and accurate packet framing rather than treating aggregate readiness evidence as a full cure for the named-segment gap.
claims_about_policy: The policy record does not support a clean compliance claim. The release-policy note requires disclosure for material limitations affecting named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and the policy text says non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending. On this record, the defensible policy position is only caveated: aggregate readiness and governance controls support certification as an operational decision, but they do not establish that the disclosure predicate has been satisfied.
concessions: The merchant dispute support segment is below target by 1.4 percentage points.
That segment is named in two marketplace renewal commitments, so the materiality concern is real on this record.
There is no admissible evidence here of completed disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or a final legal determination.
Product's non-core framing does not resolve materiality under the stated policy text.
